cells.tense: You're standing in front of something finished, and it's yours.
cells.verb: bringing a long effort all the way to a standing form
cells.place: in what gets handed on and shared
cells.ask: pick the next thing to build with the same clear hand — nothing to prove, just the choosing
cells.core:
You're standing in front of something finished, and it's yours. You set out to build it, you kept at it, and now it stands where other people can use it — a way of doing things, a body of work, a practice that didn't exist until you made it. It no longer needs you to hold it up. That's the rare part: it carries itself, and people carry it without asking whose it was.

Which leaves your hands free. If you want them to be, they're free to start again — not because anything is missing, but because you now know what finishing feels like, and you can choose the next thing from that instead of from hunger.
cells.sheetLine: You built something that stands without you, and it's being carried.

cells.tense: You're already defending how this will be remembered.
cells.verb: pressing a finished thing into permanence
cells.place: in what gets handed on and shared
cells.ask: let one person show you what they're making of what you built, and take it in without correcting it
cells.core:
You're already defending how this will be remembered. The thing is built — that part's done — but somewhere ahead there's a version where it stays exactly as you left it, and you're working to lock that in now: the right way to do it, the right words for it, who's allowed to change it. Finishing was supposed to be the end of the effort. It's turned into a second job.

What's missing isn't more holding. It's the other direction entirely: letting what you made come back to you in someone else's hands and finding out what it is now. A thing passed on changes. If you can receive one of those changes instead of fixing it, you'll know what you built is alive — and you'll be choosing the next move from a clear place rather than a clenched one.
cells.sheetLine: It's finished. You're still gripping it.

cells.tense: You finished something and never set it down where anyone could pick it up.
cells.place: in what gets handed on and shared
cells.ask: look at the thing you made, once, as finished — see it plainly before deciding anything about it
cells.core:
You finished something and never set it down where anyone could pick it up. The work is done; it's behind you, standing. But it's standing in a room nobody else has been shown into, and you're still at the door, acting as if it's unfinished or not worth the walk. Meanwhile what gets shared around you keeps forming without the thing you actually built in it.

Don't push yourself to go hand it over — that's the empty place, and effort poured straight into it just drains. Start upstream: let yourself see it. Clearly, once, with no verdict attached. What's there and what it does. Seeing it as done is what moves it from behind you to in front of you, and from there, passing it on stops being a question of courage and becomes a plain choice.
cells.sheetLine: You built it. Nobody's seen it standing.

cells.tense: You're inside something you built and calling it the weather.
cells.verb: shaping what everyone keeps and does
cells.place: in what gets handed on and shared
cells.ask: say "I made that" about one habit the people around you treat as the way it's always been
cells.core:
You're inside something you built and calling it the weather. The way things get done around you, what's repeated, what's treated as obvious — a real portion of that came from you, over years, by effort you don't remember spending. People carry it. You describe it as just how it is here, as if it arrived on its own.

The thing is finished and running. What hasn't happened is the small, earlier act underneath it: the plain statement that someone made this, and the someone was you. Not for credit — for accuracy. The moment you say out loud that it was your hands, the choosing comes back into them, and what you do next can be decided on purpose instead of by momentum.
cells.sheetLine: They're carrying what you built. You call it tradition.
